record.title: Kasumbalesa truck-driver blockade, March2019
record.direction: Import and export truck movement in both directions
record.exceptions: Small pedestrian traders resumed limited passage before the truck endpoint.
record.imposing_authority: Zambian truck drivers imposing the obstruction; bilateral authorities negotiated restoration
record.enforcement: Same-publisher contemporary onset/continuation and subsequent actual import/export restoration; no independent daily series.
record.record_type: Crossing-specific episode or qualified restriction observations
record.relationship: Different event and driver demand from the represented 2022 obstruction and 2024 government closure.
record.status_observation: Historical scoped evidence only; no status is inferred beyond the supported dated observations.
record.current_corrections: Three calendar-day difference for import/export truck passage, March23–26. Limited pedestrian passage had already resumed by March25 and is not included in this interval. The sources attribute the obstruction to drivers’ safety and harassment complaints; they do not independently adjudicate every alleged attack.
record.rationale_coding_status: Source-attributed coding accepted after separate challenge; qualifications retained
record.rationale_phase_note: Drivers explicitly demanded protection from insecurity and harassment. This is an attributed safety demand by the obstructing actors, not a certified account of each attack. The trade-protest subtype is not inferred merely because truck drivers protested; no specific trade-rule or charge demand was established.
